{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABZitCCg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhDJfHk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 55, "title": "Correct mesh geometry publication, bindings and rendered AR consumption", "body": "## Problem

At dev `af83fe8ef046ef6b7d772bc8c4e4dc32394f0bf5`, `XRMesh` publishes new geometry arrays every frame, but `TrackedSurface` compares each shape only with the preceding frame. Repeated changes below its tolerance can accumulate without advancing `lastChangedTime`. Its orientation classification can also advance mesh timestamps during rigid rotation, although XRMesh exposes no orientation attribute.

The pinned Mesh Detection Sample rebuilds geometry only when `lastChangedTime` advances. Consumers can therefore retain stale rendered geometry. `XRMesh` and `XRMeshSet` also remain publicly constructible, expose incomplete receiver/readonly/setlike bindings, and leave `detectedMeshes` without an explicit frame-brand check. See [current implementation](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/af83fe8ef046ef6b7d772bc8c4e4dc32394f0bf5/src/polyfill/api/environment.ts).

## Expected outcome

Provide coherent virtual-room mesh geometry, change notifications, bindings and tracking lifetime, demonstrated through meaningful rendered consumption on Chromium and Firefox.

Keep the exact descriptor `mesh-detection` available for Quest MR and Android AR `immersive-ar`. Preserve required-feature `NotSupportedError` rejection and optional omission for Quest VR and inline. Inline exclusion follows the pinned module; AR-only availability is emulator policy. Active frames without the feature retain empty collections.

Triangle partitions and null semantic labels remain legitimate virtual data when their geometry and usefulness are demonstrated. Universal aggregation and physical reconstruction are unnecessary for this bounded task. Other incomplete and deferred modules remain within the fixed goal.

## Context

Start from and target `dev`. Relevant dependencies are `environment.ts`, `runtime.ts`, `interface-brand.ts`, geometry/space ownership, device negotiation and the shared room used by planes, hit testing and CPU depth. Extend these together only where needed. Existing `tests/environment.ts`, `tests/reference-space-browser.ts`, `tests/firefox-upstream.ts` and application observers provide reusable tooling. The lockfile records Three.js 0.186.1, Playwright 1.64.0 and TypeScript 5.9.3.

Use [Mesh Detection 5397685](https://github.com/immersive-web/real-world-meshing/blob/539768590eb39cdff665d8e7a63f37b85eb6440b/index.bs), [Device CRD 2026-06-09](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-webxr-20260609/) and [WebIDL 622910c](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/622910c67c724e362f71e8255a0380bade261acb/index.bs).

Retain this interpretation explicitly: the mesh draft's attribute-change prose excludes pose-only timestamp changes, while its update algorithm assigns timestamps unconditionally. Follow the attribute-change interpretation already documented for planes. The correction to the existing implementation assumption is that per-frame comparison is insufficient: published geometry and its notification must agree, including cumulative changes. Any tolerance or quantization must compare against published geometry. The [pinned Sample](https://github.com/immersive-web/webxr-samples/blob/fb41c3416496974672e2c766a41c6febcba2d07e/proposals/mesh-detection.html) establishes the consumer impact. The analogous pinned WPT plane timestamp test corroborates the plane interpretation; it is not a mesh behavioral test.

Earlier #19/#20 introduced triangle meshes; #51/#52 corrected planes. Neither completed this mesh scope. Historical mesh execution reports 128 callbacks and 100 meshes per AR profile on Chromium, without pinned application provenance or demonstrated update rendering. Existing test code and merged PRs do not establish these missing outcomes. Dev Actions currently reports zero runs.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Complete `XRMesh` and `XRMeshSet` bindings: public construction throws `TypeError`; readonly attributes use branded prototype getters; `meshSpace` preserves SameObject identity. Reject forged receivers and proxies while accepting genuine separately injected same-origin objects through borrowed getters/methods. Keep mutable backing tracking state inaccessible through public mesh fields or writable registry entries.
- [ ] Implement readonly setlike behavior: insertion order, size, paired entries, `keys === values === Symbol.iterator`, appropriate descriptors, callback arguments/thisArg, exception propagation and callback validation even for empty sets. `has()` converts its XRMesh argument and rejects invalid values with `TypeError`; a genuine nonmember mesh returns false. Expose no collection mutators.
- [ ] Make `detectedMeshes` reject invalid receivers with `TypeError` before frame-state checks. Genuine inactive-frame access throws `InvalidStateError`. Preserve supported negotiation, empty unenabled collections, session-owned mesh spaces and foreign-session pose-query `InvalidStateError` behavior.
- [ ] Publish indexed geometry and timestamps coherently. Unchanged geometry and rigid translation/rotation do not advance shape timestamps. Shape/topology changes advance timestamps when published. Repeated individually small changes eventually publish an updated shape and timestamp; prevent silent cumulative drift. Document any precision policy. Do not invent SameObject guarantees for vertices/indices, which lack that annotation. Writable exported arrays must not corrupt internal change comparisons, room sensing or another session.
- [ ] Independently reconstruct indexed and nonindexed rectangular, sloped and degenerate fixtures from vertices plus meshSpace. Check finite metre coordinates, valid indices, normal-aligned +Y and world-space agreement within `1e-4` metres for known valid fixtures. Measure packaged-room coverage and describe partition limitations. Preserve tracking identity and frame membership snapshots; exercise unavailable poses, removal, reacquisition and shutdown. Under the existing emulator policy, removed spaces return null from valid owning-frame pose queries; reacquisition/restart uses fresh identities and leaves no stale tracking or presentation resources.
- [ ] Execute the unchanged pinned `proposals/mesh-detection.html` Sample on Quest MR and Android AR in both Chromium and Firefox through the actual extension and genuine panel route: four combinations. Demonstrate identifiable mesh pixels in both Quest eyes or Android's mono view, independently checked room alignment and viewer movement. Through disclosed controlled virtual-backend updates, demonstrate actual consumer geometry rebuilds after shape changes, pose movement without false shape notifications, removal/reacquisition and end/restart. Keep application logic/results unchanged; its existing optional overlay checkbox may be disabled. This earns WebXR Samples evidence, not an additional official Three.js application count.
- [ ] Extend the existing browser driver with documented mesh contract/application selections; these selectors do not yet exist. Run those focused selections on both browsers, `npm run build:firefox` (including typecheck/build), and `npm run test:environment`. Preserve affected plane geometry, mesh hit intersections and CPU-depth calibration through targeted assertions appropriate to shared changes. The Coordinator owns implementation, tests and normal PR review; add no independent AI re-review or generic suite rerun.
- [ ] Update the inventory and reproduction documentation with commands, exact browser/tool/application/dependency versions and hashes, instrumentation, measurements, captures, failures, skips and unperformed checks. Keep historical execution separate. If an AI-authored requirement proves mistaken, retain its original assumption, correction, pinned primary evidence and rationale in the Issue/PR; correct it without human approval or independent AI re-review while preserving the goal and meaningful acceptance.

## Optional validation

Additional room fixtures, longer deformation sequences or another pinned mesh consumer. No unrelated application rerun is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WebXR API compatibility goal for
Quest 3 VR/MR and Android AR. Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance
criteria when primary specifications or measured evidence establish the correction.
Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
